articles.title: Green Place lança produto que auxilia combate à mosca-da-fruta | G1
articles.standfirst: Tecnologia mistura cinco óleos essenciais com ação repelente e desalojante.
articles.summary: Tecnologia mistura cinco óleos essenciais com ação repelente e desalojante.
articles.body:
4_ Produto da Green Place reúne cinco óleos essenciais com efeito repelente e desalojante _ Seiva do Vale — Foto: Acervo/Seiva do Vale

Um novo produto está sendo introduzido no mercado com a promessa de revolucionar o controle de insetos, inclusive da temida mosca-da-fruta, ao potencializar a ação de inseticidas. O Traçador é uma solução inovadora à base de óleos essenciais desenvolvida pela Green Place, que atua como adjuvante, ou seja, potencializar o efeito de inseticidas, tanto químicos quanto biológicos.

O produto é uma mistura de cinco óleos essenciais, todos derivados de plantas e extratos vegetais. Esses cinco ativos formam uma combinação projetada para atuar como um potente adjuvante. Isso porque eles vão combinar um efeito repelente e desalojante, garantindo a máxima eficácia de proteção.

A ação combinada dos óleos essenciais garante uma alta efetividade no auxílio do controle de insetos. O Traçador une a tecnologia de aplicação com a bioatividade de seus óleos essenciais para maximizar os efeitos dos produtos químicos, resultando em uma melhoria significativa na eficiência do controle e manejo de insetos.

articles.title: Black sunflower art raises awareness of the war in Ukraine
articles.summary: The artwork in Bristol commemorates those who have died on both sides of the conflict.
articles.body:
An artist who has been painting sunflowers black says he hopes the work will help raise awareness about the war in Ukraine.

About 100 sunflowers were planted by artist Duncan McKellar on a plot of lawn next to Bristol's City Hall.

McKellar planted the flowers as a "guerilla artwork memorial" last year but has since been given permission and is painting the plants black as they naturally die as a way of further raising awareness of the conflict.

"Black itself is synonymous with death, the flowers themselves have died and they're arranged in a grid which is intended to look like war graves," said McKellar of his artwork entitled Flowers for the Fallen.

Statue commemorates miners who died in explosion

City's u-turn on van dwellers' council tax

Homeless families given alternative to hotel living

McKellar says that he plans to use the black painted flowers as the basis for a planned exhibition in February, which will mark the fifth anniversary of the war.

The artist says the work is intended to commemorate people that have died on both sides of the conflict.

Neither side publishes their casualty figures, but estimates put the total losses from both Russia and Ukraine in the hundreds of thousands.

Western support and public attention for the war has fluctuated over the previous four years.

Zhenya Alshkil is a Ukrainian living in Bath who founded a group called Friends of Oleksandriya, which has been supporting Ukraine and Ukrainian refugees living in the UK since the start of the war.

Alshkil says that "British people have done a lot" for Ukraine but says the war continues to escalate.

"Many Ukrainians went back home [over the summer] because there is a strong pull to go home and also fathers could be fighting or they can't leave Ukraine because they're under 60 and there is martial law which stops them from joining their families here," she said.

"Many of them came back just now and they're in a very poor state, the situation escalated on 27 August.

"The drone attacks lasted almost non-stop apart from a few days when Americans came for peace talks, but otherwise Kyiv is under fire all the time."

Alshkil has put on a number of cultural events and art installations in Bath and says they are a great way to build positive cultural ties and help support her country from the UK.

McKellar says he hopes his work can also help put Ukraine back in to people's minds.

"I don't think many people are walking down Park Street thinking about Ukraine but hopefully as they hit College Green that thought would be put back into their head," he said.

articles.title: Europa reacciona a tiempo y firma las tablas en el arranque de la Solheim
articles.standfirst: Estados Unidos ganó los dos primeros partidos y las europeas, los dos últimos
articles.summary: Estados Unidos ganó los dos primeros partidos y las europeas, los dos últimos
articles.body: Europa evitó que Estados Unidos volviera a tomar una ventaja importante desde la primera sesión de la Solheim Cup. Después de ver cómo las norteamericanas se adjudicaban los dos primeros foursomes de la mañana en Bernardus Golf, el equipo de Anna Nordqvist reaccionó a tiempo con los triunfos de Maja Stark y Linn Grant y de Leona Maguire y Esther Henseleit para alcanzar los fourballs de la tarde con empate, 2-2. Un resultado importante para las europeas, que hace dos años, en Virginia, comenzaron la defensa del título cediendo por 3-1 en los foursomes y terminaron la primera jornada con un preocupante 6-2. Esta vez, aunque Estados Unidos volvió a golpear primero, la respuesta llegó antes. Nelly Korda y Allisen Corpuz fueron las encargadas de colocar el primer punto estadounidense. La número uno del mundo y su compañera, una pareja que no conoce la derrota en este formato (establecieron un nuevo récord con cinco triunfos en cinco pàrtidos, sin empates), castigaron prácticamente cada error de Charley Hull y Lottie Woad. La debutante europea tuvo un estreno prometedor, embocando un birdie en el primer hoyo, pero las estadounidenses fueron tomando el control hasta situarse 5 arriba después del 13. Hull y Woad prolongaron el partido, aunque terminaron cayendo por 4&3. Poco después llegó el segundo golpe. Nanna Koerstz Madsen y Céline Boutier comenzaron por delante, pero fueron perdiendo consistencia conforme avanzaba la mañana. Alison Lee y Lauren Coughlin aprovecharon sus oportunidades, se pusieron por delante en el 8 y terminaron cerrando su victoria por 3&2. Europa estaba 0-2 y empezaba a mirar con preocupación los dos partidos que quedaban en el campo. La reacción llegó desde Suecia. Maja Stark y Linn Grant fueron la pareja europea más convincente de la mañana. Llegaron a estar cuatro arriba después de siete hoyos y Grant protagonizó uno de los golpes de la sesión embocando directamente desde el bunker en el 9 para salvar el empate en el hoyo. Rose Zhang y Jennifer Kupcho reaccionaron ganando el 10 y el 11, pero las suecas no se descompusieron. Resistieron el intento de remontada estadounidense y aprovecharon los errores de Zhang, que encontró el agua en el 15 y volvió a hacerlo en su segundo golpe del 16 cuando necesitaba atacar el green. Grant embocó el putt definitivo para el 3&2 que devolvía a Europa al partido. Todo quedaba entonces en manos de Henseleit y Maguire. La alemana y la irlandesa llegaron dos arriba al 16 frente a Andrea Lee y Lindy Duncan, pero una salida al agua de Henseleit permitió a Estados Unidos recortar distancias. Así que el 17 terminó siendo decisivo. Maguire, una de las grandes especialistas europeas en esta competición, se inventó una extraordinaria recuperación desde una posición muy complicada para dejar a Henseleit la posibilidad de salvar el par. Europa llegó uno arriba al último y allí la alemana se resarció definitivamente de su error anterior: salida perfecta a calle y un magnífico golpe alrededor de green que dejó el hoyo prácticamente sentenciado. Victoria por 2 arriba y tablas después de casi cinco horas de foursomes. La Solheim vuelve a la casilla de salida con 2-2. La sesión vespertina, en modalidad fourball (cuatro bolas en juego en cada partido) supondrá además el estreno de la representación española en esta Solheim Cup. Carlota Ciganda, que descansó durante los foursomes matinales, formará pareja a partir de las 13.50 horas con la debutante Julia López Ramírez en un duelo de máxima exigencia frente a Nelly Korda y Lauren Coughlin, dos de las jugadoras que ya sumaron un punto para Estados Unidos por la mañana. Antes, a las 13.05, Charley Hull y Lottie Woad repetirán juntas frente a Yealimi Noh y Angel Yin. A las 13.20 jugarán Céline Boutier y Nanna Koerstz Madsen contra Megan Khang y Alison Lee, mientras que a las 13.35 llegará el estreno de Mimi Rhodes y Nastasia Nadaud frente a Allisen Corpuz y Auston Kim. Todas las miradas españolas, sin embargo, estarán puestas en el último partido. Ciganda, una de las grandes veteranas de Europa, ejercerá de guía de Julia López Ramírez en su primera experiencia en la Solheim. Y enfrente estará nada menos que la número uno del mundo...

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers makes uncomfortable Packers admission ahead of retirement
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers could have one final chance to return to the team where he started before ending his playing career, making a potential appearance at Lambeau F...
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers could have one final chance to return to the team where he started before ending his playing career, making a potential appearance at Lambeau Field especially meaningful. His time with the Green Bay Packers produced the defining achievements of his career, including four league MVP awards and a Super Bowl title.

With Rodgers preparing to retire after the 2026 season, a return to Lambeau Field could have been a fitting way to close that chapter. However, Rodgers has indicated that coming back to Green Bay in another role may not be something he is interested in. He would still welcome an invitation from the Packers, but he acknowledged that it may never come.

"I think there's some people that have a lot of affection for me, and I would assume we're talking four or five years from now that there will be fans who still have appreciation for what I've done, especially after so much time has passed," commented the former Packers superstar via ESPN's Rob Demovsky.

Aaron Rodgers time with the Green Bay Packers

Only a handful of figures from Rodgers' time in Green Bay remain with the organization , including general manager Brian Gutekunst and head coach Matt LaFleur. Rodgers' relationship with Gutekunst became strained near the end of his Packers tenure, with the general manager ultimately sending him to the New York Jets .

"I think there's certain people in the building who wouldn't be totally on board, and maybe I wouldn't be on board if they were still there as well."

Even with the way his departure played out, Rodgers does not want that chapter of his career to overshadow everything he accomplished in Green Bay. He still values the relationships he built during his time with the Packers and the friendships he formed along the way.

"I loved my time there. And I didn't let the ending skew any of the good times that we had and how much I enjoyed playing there and playing at Lambeau and being around so many great people over the years."

CLINTONVILLE - The Spartans defeated the Truckers 25-14, 25-15, 25-13 to improve to 10-7 overall and 2-0 in the North Eastern Conference.

Luxemburg-Casco was led by Claire Schlies with 16 assists and six digs; Aubrey Frey with 15 kills, six digs and five aces; Stella Schleis with 11 assists; and Cayden Hruska with six digs and six aces.

"Credit to Clintonville, they were scrappy and pushed us in the first set and really all night," Luxemburg-Casco coach Jeff Frey said. "Proud of our girls to not get frustrated and stay the course. It's always great to get a win on the road."

articles.title: Taunton's grassroots football 'at breaking point' after closures
articles.summary: Some sports pitches had to be closed after the dry summer damaged the grass.
articles.body:
Grassroots football is at risk after damage from extreme heat in recent months led to the closure of some pitches, a football expert has said.

Taunton Town Council closed its sports pitches to "protect the long-term quality and sustainability of the facilities" and to help ensure player safety.

Paul Coltman, a football consultant who works with the affected clubs, said this would not only affect organised matches but also training and recreational football.

"We're already close to breaking point with more teams than we have pitches," he said. "Those pitches that are still usable will now have more games on them which means the knock-on effect is huge."

New summer music event aims to boost town's economy

Tourist tax likely as visitors 'need to contribute'

Why shining a laser at an air ambulance could be 'catastrophic'

The pitches run by the council include Galmington Park, Hamilton Park, Priorswood Park, Taunton Green and Victoria Park.

"This is a huge impact on local football and a massive drain on an already shrinking volunteer base," Coltman said.

The council said the extended drought had weakened the grass cover and hardened the playing surfaces.

"Our inspections have indicated that continued use at this stage could cause significant damage to the pitches and affect their condition for the remainder of the season," a spokesperson for the council said.

"Whilst the pitches are showing signs of recovery, they remain under considerable stress and require additional time to recover fully before regular play resumes."

Coltman said the pitches were already in decline before the hot weather affected them further.

"This is a result of years of neglect and poor maintenance," he said.

"We're really lucky locally that we have wonderful clubs across grassroots football.

"Those clubs are now going to need to work together to find alternative venues.

"This isn't going to go away quickly by the sound of things."

The council spokesperson said the closure was not indefinite.

"The pitches are being inspected regularly and the situation is reviewed on a week-by-week basis," the spokesperson said.

"We are keen to reopen the facilities as soon as conditions allow and are working closely with clubs and leagues to keep them updated."

articles.title: Solheim Cup: How Team Europe and Team USA stars embraced first-tee party and 'insane' atmosphere at Bernardus Golf
articles.summary: What was the first-tee atmosphere like at the Solheim Cup? How a party atmosphere at Bernardus Golf brought an entertaining start to Team Europe's bid to regain the trophy in the Netherlands; watch the Solheim Cup live on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
The horseshoe-shaped grandstand around the first tee at Bernardus Golf was close to capacity long before daylight, with nearly 3,000 spectators - and plenty more along the fairway - creating a party-like atmosphere of noise and excitement.

United States captain Angela Stanford danced onto the tee after emerging from the tunnel, a walk Charley Hull said earlier in the week was like 'entering an arena', with vice-captains - from both sides - doing their best to make things even louder.

One sign on display read 'Dutch courage, European glory', with the Netherlands doing the players proud by creating a boisterous environment more akin to a football stadium or darts event than a golf course.

Nordqvist's vice-captain Anne van Dam grabbed the microphone to guide the crowd through "Links Rechts", the song that became the unofficial anthem for the Dutch football team during the World Cup and involves lots of bouncing in a certain direction.

"It doesn't get better than this," Nordqvist said about the atmosphere. "The crowds are amazing. I don't think I've ever seen this many Europeans on the first tee."

Stands full of fans dressed in banana costumes, stars and stripes suits and golf bucket hats all jumping together at 7.20am was a brilliantly bonkers scene, with the dancing and singing only increasing as they edged closer to play getting under way.

"Let's go Europe, let's go!" chants echoed around the grandstand before Europe's classic 'Final Countdown' blasted out of the speakers, with Team USA's star-studded opening pairing arriving almost 10 minutes early to soak up the atmosphere.

Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz were quickly joined by Hull and rookie Lottie Woad, with every pair's arrival greeted with smoke cannons, huge cheers and cleverly thought-out adaptations of chants heard in other sports.

A big message of 'quiet please' appeared on the big screens ahead of the opening tee shots, with a Corpuz-inspired adaptation of the Beatles classic 'Hey Jude' quickly cut for respectful silence as players hit their drives.

The party at the tee continued long after Woad rolled in the opening birdie of the event on the first green, with Team USA vice-captain Paula Creamer - wearing her cowboy hat - and fan favourite Megan Khang among those showcasing their dance moves.

"Ohhhh, Leona Maguire" was sung loudly to the tune of Kings of Leon's 'Sex on Fire', while Desmond Decker's 'Israelites' was adapted to fit in Esther Henseleit's name.

Remember the "Europe's on fire, USA is terrified" song chanted regularly during last year's Ryder Cup win at Bethpage Black? A Maguire twist was heard to recognise the Irishwoman with one of the best winning percentages in Solheim Cup history.

Carlota Ciganda was the only European player with previous experience who sat out the opening session, but the Spaniard was sporting a Solheim Cup beanie and showing the rookies how to enjoy every second of their week.

Dancing along to every song, arm in arm with the debutants during 'It's Raining Men' and when the DJ played a Vengaboys track, the Solheim stalwart seemed to never have anything but a huge grin on her face.

The positive vibes spread throughout the European team, with Maja Stark and Linn Grant running out to the crowd and swaying their hips to ABBA's karaoke classic 'Dancing Queen' as they awaited their match to get going.

"These people absolutely make it for the players," said Dame Laura Davies, a 12-time Solheim Cup player, said about the crowd. "Without these brilliant fans, it's just not the same."

"Maja Stark, doo-doo, doo-doo, doo-doo" - to the theme of Baby Shark - is an earworm nobody needs but works well with the Swede's name, with Stark and Linn Grant buoyed by the crowds to earn Team Europe's first point of the contest.

The weather turning from early sunshine to persistent light rain didn't dampen the spirits of those following the action, with strong galleries lining the fairways to watch a tight opening session that left the teams tied at two apiece.

"We had incredible support out here," Maguire said after her win. "They were really spurring us on, especially when that weather got bad and miserable. It was that extra little bit we needed to grind it out."

The noise appeared to reach even higher levels during the afternoon session, where former major winner Karen Stupples described the crowds as 'insane'. If the quality of golf on the course matches the atmosphere being created off it, the 20th edition of the Solheim Cup could be one of the most memorable yet.

articles.title: Amgen Irish Open: Shane Lowry fires course record to top leaderboard as Rory McIlroy left feeling putting 'frustration'
articles.summary: Shane Lowry stormed clear at the Amgen Irish Open with a course-record 62; Rory McIlroy sits nine strokes back
articles.body:
Lowry mixed nine birdies with a lone bogey during a brilliant eight-under 62 at Trump International Golf Links & Hotel, lifting him to 11 under and three strokes clear of the rest of the morning starters.

The former Open champion's closest challenge from his half of the field came from Haotong Li and Jacob Skov Olesen, who posted rounds of 63 and 64 respectively to move to eight under, with Tom McKibbin among those six strokes back.

Patrick Reed heads into the weekend on four under, with Jon Rahm and Robert MacIntyre another shot adrift, with Rory McIlroy nine off the halfway lead after struggling on the greens during a second successive 69.

First-round leader Joaquin Niemann and England's Tyrrell Hatton were among the later starters.

Lowry, who won this tournament in 2009 as a 22-year-old amateur, was playing in the group behind McIlroy and saw crowds for him grow after a run of three consecutive birdies from the third.

He holed a long-range putt at the seventh and picked up further shots over the next two holes to race to the turn in 30, then added back-to-back birdies from the 11th to leave Lowry briefly on '59 watch'.

Lowry's hopes of a sub-60 round suffered a setback with a three-putt bogey from 20 feet at the 13th, although he bounced back by birdieing the 15th and closed out his record-breaking round with three straight pars.

"It was real fun out there," Lowry said. "I got off to a nice start and then I just kept going. I felt great out there. Just kept my foot on the gas and tried to keep hitting good shots and keep holing putts."

Work to do for McIlroy after putting 'frustration'

McIlroy holed a birdie from off the second green but failed to take advantage of multiple chances on his front nine, with the world No 2 failing to get up and down from the sand and missing a close-range putt to save par at the seventh.

The Masters champion responded with a sensational eagle at the par-five eighth, firing his approach close, only to card a sloppy bogey at the 11th and cancel out a long-range birdie at the 17th with a disappointing three-putt at the last.

"Frustration," was McIlroy's assessment of his second round. "I just didn't have it on the greens. I really struggled to read them. It's hard whenever you struggle to read them.

"It's been a tough one on the greens the last two days, but tee to green I've actually been pretty happy with how everything else is. I just need to try to hole a few more over the weekend."

MacIntyre carded a 65 to stand at three under but five-time major champion Koepka - who followed his opening round of 75 with 66 - was in danger of missing the cut at one over.

articles.title: Irish Open: Superb Shane Lowry surges clear as Rory McIlroy struggles at Doonbeg
articles.summary: Shane Lowry cards a course-record 62 to take control of the Irish Open as putting woes prevent defending champion Rory McIlroy from making a second-round charge in Doonbeg.
articles.body:
Shane Lowry carded a course-record 62 to take control of the Irish Open as putting woes prevented defending champion Rory McIlroy from making a second-round charge at Doonbeg.

Irishman Lowry, who won his national title as an amateur in 2009, made six birdies in the space of seven holes on his front nine to surge clear in more favourable conditions after Thursday's heavy wind and rain.

Three more birdies - and a bogey on 13 - followed as the 39-year-old established a three-shot lead over China's Li Haotong and Denmark's Jacob Skov Olesen at Trump International Golf Links in County Clare on the west coast of the Republic of Ireland.

"It was real fun out there. I got off to a nice start and then I just kept going," said Lowry, who is playing his first tournament since failing to make the final two PGA Tour play-off events.

"I felt great out there. Just kept my foot on the gas and tried to keep hitting good shots and keep holing putts and it was a nice day."

Irish Open second round as it happened - Lowry breaks course record

With all parts of his game operating efficiently, Lowry started with two pars before reeling off a hat-trick of birdies from the third.

After a par on the sixth, the 2019 Open champion drained a 24-foot putt for a birdie two on the next and closed out his front nine with two more birdies to turn in six-under 30.

Lowry, who has not won an individual title in four years, scrambled for a par five at 10 when he hacked out of long rough before holing a 10-footer.

Birdies at 11 and 12 ignited hopes of a 59 at the par-70 venue before a sloppy bogey on 13 when he three-putted from 18 feet.

But the world number 53, who attracted large galleries around the spectacular links course, rolled in a 19-footer for birdie at 15 to return to -11 before finishing with three pars.

"I thought about it," Lowry, who has not returned a top-20 finish since February, said when asked if a sub-60 round entered his mind.

"Yeah, I did think about it until I three-putted 13. No, I did have a little laugh. Out in 30 and the back nine is only 34, so, yeah, you do kind of think about it a little bit."

He added: "I know I made a little mistake on 13, but I think I did a good job after that of playing the rest of the round really well and giving myself a couple of chances on the way in."

While Lowry prospered in more benign conditions, his good friend and Ryder Cup team-mate McIlroy failed to climb the leaderboard as he finished the day nine shots back.

Six-time major winner McIlroy, who is chasing a third Irish Open triumph, was even par for his round before a stunning fairway metal from 267 yards to two feet set up an eagle three at the eighth.

That moment of brilliance failed to ignite McIlroy's challenge, however, as he bogeyed the 11th and missed a series of birdie putts before sinking a 40-footer to pick up a shot at the 17th.

Northern Ireland's McIlroy looked set for a birdie-birdie finish after firing his approach at the final hole to four feet, but he took three putts to drop a shot and card a second consecutive 69.

"I just didn't have it on the greens. I really struggled to read them," said McIlroy.

He added: "It's been a tough one on the greens the last two days. But tee to green I've actually been pretty happy with how everything else is. I just need to try to hole a few more over the weekend."

With the late groups still to complete their rounds, Li and Olesen established themselves as Lowry's closest challengers.

Li, who finished tied fourth in last year's Open Championship at Royal Portrush, carded seven birdies, an eagle and two bogeys to shoot 63, while Olesen mixed seven birdies with a single bogey in a 64.

Northern Ireland's Tom McKibbin shaved a shot off his opening 68 to reach five under, a group which includes Scotland's Ewen Ferguson (66) and 2024 winner Rasmus Hojgaard (63).

Playing with McIlroy, Scotland's Robert MacIntyre bounced back from an opening 72 with a fine 65 to sit eight shots back alongside two-time winner Jon Rahm, who recorded four birdies in a 67.

Race to Dubai leader and 2018 Masters winner Patrick Reed is one shot better off on four under, but five-time major champion Brooks Koepka needed a birdie on 18 to shoot 66 and sneak inside the projected cut line on one over.

articles.title: Carlota sostiene a Europa en un último hoyo de infarto y la Solheim sigue empatada
articles.standfirst: La navarra salvó medio punto cuando todo parecía ya decidido para Korda y Coughlin
articles.summary: La navarra salvó medio punto cuando todo parecía ya decidido para Korda y Coughlin
articles.body: Carlota Ciganda volvió a vestirse de heroína para Europa. Tres años después de convertirse en la pesadilla de Nelly Korda en Finca Cortesín, la navarra volvió a cruzarse en el camino de la número uno del mundo para rescatar, esta vez junto a la debutante Julia López Ramírez, un medio punto que permite al equipo europeo cerrar empatado (4-4) el primer día de la Solheim Cup. Y lo hizo de una manera casi agónica: con un eagle espectacular desde unos nueve metros en el 16 para devolver su partido ante Korda y Lauren Coughlin a las tablas y embocando un putt de media distancia en el 18 para salvar el par cuando prácticamente todo parecía perdido. Fue el último golpe del viernes. El que decidió que nadie durmiera por delante en Bernardus Golf. Carlota y Julia habían construido un partido magnífico ante una de las parejas más poderosas de Estados Unidos. La rookie española dejó claro desde el primer tee que no había acudido a Países Bajos simplemente a acompañar a una de las grandes referentes europeas. Salió bailando, sonriente, y después respondió con golf. En el 4, Korda embocó primero el birdie y Julia contestó inmediatamente con el suyo. Y en el par cuatro corto del 8 firmó uno de los golpes de la tarde, alcanzando el green desde el tee para ganar el hoyo con birdie y colocar a las españolas dos arriba después de que Carlota hubiera ganado el 6 y el 7. La ventaja se mantuvo hasta el 10, pero Coughlin cambió el partido. Embocó un espectacular birdie desde unos 15 metros en el par tres del 11 y volvió a ganar el 12, donde Julia mandó al agua un golpe cargado de efecto. Estados Unidos ganó también el 13 y, en apenas tres hoyos, las españolas pasaron de dominar por dos a estar uno abajo. Julia apareció entonces para salvar un par fundamental en el 14. Carlota rozó el birdie desde unos 18 metros en el 15 y llegó el 16. Nelly se quedó corta con su approach y encontró el agua. Ciganda había colocado un magnífico segundo golpe en green y se enfrentaba a un putt de eagle de unos nueve metros, con caída de izquierda a derecha. Lo embocó. Puño al aire, rugido europeo y partido empatado. En el 17 tuvo incluso la oportunidad de completar la remontada. Korda falló desde unos nueve metros y Carlota dispuso después de un putt para poner a Europa uno arriba. La bola se escapó por abajo y la navarra terminó de rodillas sobre el green lamentando una ocasión que parecía decisiva. Pero el tiempo demostró que no lo era, ni mucho menos. Quedaba todavía un último capítulo. El 18 arrancó convertido en una pesadilla para las españolas, fallando sus respectivos golpes desde el tee. Julia encontró el búnker de calle de la derecha y Carlota se marchó muy abierta al mismo lado. Korda, con madera tres, y Coughlin, con driver, no tuvieron problemas para situarse en el centro de la calle. No contentas con eso, las españolas volvieron a equivocarse haciendo que la situación se convirtiera ya en dramática. Carlota mandó su segundo golpe muy a la derecha, detrás de los árboles y del camino de espectadores. Julia intentó salir del búnker, golpeó el talud y la bola regresó prácticamente al mismo sitio. Consiguió sacarla en el siguiente intento, pero su bola quedó ya fuera de la pelea por el hoyo. Así que desde ese momento, ya todo dependía de Ciganda. Korda se dejó unos cuatro metros para birdie y Coughlin tuvo una oportunidad incluso más cercana para ganar el partido. Ciganda, por su parte, consiguió fabricar desde su posición comprometida una opción de par de unos cuatro metros y medio. Primero falló Korda. Después tampoco entró el birdie de Coughlin. Turno para la navarra. si fallaba, Estados Unidos ganaba el partido y cerraba el viernes 4,5-3,5. Si embocaba, Europa salvaba el empate. Y Ciganda no tembló. Bola al centro y medio punto europeo. Antes, la sesión de fourballs había dejado una victoria para cada equipo y dos empates. Megan Khang y Alison Lee remontaron un partido que Boutier y Madsen dominaban por dos después de cinco hoyos para imponerse por un contundente 5&3. Mimi Rhodes y Nastasia Nadaud, dos rookies lanzadas juntas por Anna Nordqvist, respondieron con una fantástica victoria por 2&1 ante Allisen Corpuz y Auston Kim. También acabó empatado el duelo entre Charley Hull y Lottie Woad y Yealimi Noh y Angel Yin. Europa llegó dos veces a estar tres arriba y Woad ofreció momentos magníficos, con cuatro birdies consecutivos entre el 2 y el 5 y un eagle en el 10, pero Estados Unidos reaccionó y llevó el partido hasta el 18. Allí Woad rozó un larguísimo birdie para ganar y Noh tampoco convirtió después su oportunidad. Después del 2-2 de los foursomes matinales, los fourballs dejaron otro 2-2. Ocho partidos, cuatro puntos para cada equipo. Europa y Estados Unidos se fueron de Bernardus como habían llegado: sin que nadie pudiera separarles. Pero eso sí, con un subidón anímico final para las anfitrionas. Porque si el marcador continuó equilibrado fue, sobre todo, porque cuando el viernes entero quedó reducido a un putt, el último golpe del día, Carlota Ciganda volvió a aparecer.

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: Team Europe and Team USA tied 4-4 after tight opening day and Carlota Ciganda's dramatic finish
articles.summary: Team Europe and Team USA are tied after the opening day for just the second time in Solheim Cup history; Carlota Ciganda's late par-save ensured both teams claimed two points in both sessions at Bernardus Golf; watch day two live on Saturday from 6am on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Both teams claimed a share of the spoils in the morning foursomes before producing a repeat result in the afternoon session, as Angela Stanford's American side looked set to hold an opening-day lead until Ciganda's impressive finish.

Ciganda nailed a 15-foot par-save with the final shot of a thrilling day at Bernardus Golf, seeing her and rookie Julia Lopez Ramirez scramble a half-point against world No 1 Nelly Korda and Lauren Coughlin.

Anna Nordqvist had elected to stick with the same two pairings beaten in the tied foursomes session to lead out Team Europe again in the afternoon, with Celine Boutier and Nanna Koerstz Madsen thrashed 5&3 by Megan Khang and Alison Lee.

Hull and Woad appeared to be closing towards their first win together when they moved three up with seven holes to play, only for Yealimi Noh and Angel Yin to battle back and grab a share of the spoils.

Rookies Mimi Rhodes and Nastasia Nadaud made the dream start to their Solheim Cup careers by despatching Allisen Corpuz and Auston Kim 2&1, while Ciganda and Lopez Ramirez's late half-point leaves the contest level after the opening day for just the second time in its history.

"I think not losing today is important," Ciganda said. "It's 4-4 for the day, so big momentum going into tomorrow. Hopefully we can take that into tomorrow's foursomes and win both the morning and afternoon sides."

Europe locked with USA in Solheim thriller

Woad did the early heavy-lifting for her and Hull in the fourballs opener, responding to Noh birdieing the opening hole by winning three consecutive holes from the third.

Hull drained a long-range birdie at the sixth to move the European pair three clear, with Team USA winning the next two holes before Woad posted an eagle at the par-five 10th and Hull claimed the next.

Noh holed a 12-footer at the 12th to start successive birdies and almost holed her tee shot at the par-three 15th, then delivered a clutch birdie at the 17th and matched Hull's par at the last.

"It was a very good match," Woad insisted. "We had the lead for most of it, but they kept on fighting back. I think overall we played great but that putt on the last kind of described the back nine, I would say."

Boutier and Madsen were two up after five holes but couldn't keep up with a dominant pair, as Khang and Lee played the next eight-hole stretch in eight under to secure Team USA their first point of the session.

Khang's victory is her sixth consecutive Solheim Cup match won and leaves her unbeaten in nine matches, a run stretching back since 2021 and the second-longest streak in history.

"It's always nice seeing a big bird (eagle) and it definitely took the lid off for us," Khang said. "It was definitely a ham-and-egg session on the back nine. She's such a great partner."

Rhodes and Nadaud fully justified their captain's picks as they earned Europe's only full point of the afternoon session, before full focus turned to Korda and Coughlin being dragged into a final-hole tussle.

Korda and Coughlin recovered from being two down with eight to play to win three consecutive holes and edge ahead, before Ciganda produced a key birdie at the 16th.

Both Korda and Coughlin left birdie putts short on the 18th green, then watched on as Ciganda recovered from two wayward shots to salvage a par and spark wild celebrations from the European team.

Sky Sports Golf will have at least 12 hours of live coverage from the first two days, with coverage continuing on Saturday at 6am ahead of the opening foursomes match teeing off at 6.40am (7.40am local time).

The afternoon fourballs are scheduled to start at 12.05pm UK time, with coverage continuing until after the final putt is holed, while Sunday singles coverage begins at 9am on Sky Sports Golf ahead of the opening tee shot at 10.10am.

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: Carlota Ciganda lifts Europe to a 4-4 tie with US on opening day
articles.summary: Carlota Ciganda steals the show after Europe's top pairing of Charley Hull and Lottie Woad fail to ignite on day one of the Solheim Cup against the United States.
articles.body:
Carlota Ciganda once again stole the show after Europe's top pairing of Charley Hull and Lottie Woad failed to ignite against the USA on the opening day of the Solheim Cup.

The 36-year-old Spaniard - the oldest player on show this weekend - let out a roar after holing a 15-foot putt to earn Europe an unlikely half point in the final fourball match of the day and ensure honours are even at 4-4 heading into Saturday.

Ciganda's celebration evoked memories of the nerve-shredding finale at Finca Cortesin in 2023, when her putt allowed Europe to retain the trophy with a 14-14 tie.

And once again Nelly Korda, beaten by Ciganda in Spain three years ago, was on the receiving end.

The world number one and her playing partner Lauren Coughlin both left match-winning putts short to allow Ciganda, who had crucially won the 16th hole with an eagle, to deliver a stunning reprieve for Anna Nordqvist's team at Bernardus Golf Club in the Netherlands.

"I love this week. I just love playing for the team, for my team-mates. We fought hard and we got half a point, which is important," said Ciganda, who is playing in her eighth Solheim Cup.

"It gives us big momentum and hopefully we can take that into and win both [of Saturday's] morning and afternoon sessions."

European hopes of parity had begun to fade into the shadows of the evening sunshine, with Angela Stanford's visitors seemingly assuming control of the 20th edition of the biggest team competition in women's golf.

It proved to be a hard-fought opening day between Europe and a US team looking to retain the trophy following their 15½-12½ victory in Virginia two years ago.

However, despite Ciganda's heroics, there was also a sense of what might have been for the hosts, who found themselves 6-2 behind at this stage two years ago at the Robert Trent Jones Golf Club.

History has shown a good start to be essential in this competition, with the team holding the advantage after the opening day taking home the trophy 14 out of 19 times.

And the decision to send out Hull and Woad first in both the morning foursomes and the afternoon fourballs failed to deliver the impetus Europe's captain Nordqvist would have hoped for.

When Hull and rookie Woad emerged on the raucous opening tee with daylight barely breaking through at 06:40 BST, they did so as the two highest-ranked players in the European side at eight and seven respectively.

Yet despite winning the opening hole, Nordqvist's gamble never looked like paying off against the formidable pairing of Korda and Allisen Corpuz.

The American duo won all four of their foursomes matches across the previous two editions of this contest and became the first to make it five on the spin with a comfortable 4&3 victory.

Disappointingly for Europe, Hull and Woad then let a three-hole advantage slip on the back nine on Friday afternoon against Yealimi Noh and Angel Yin, who was playing only her third competitive round since June.

They did at least scramble a half point despite loud music being played by an on-course DJ clearly distracting Woad and Noh as they lined up their final putts. BBC Sport has contacted the Ladies European Tour about the incident which clouded the end of a pulsating match.

In contrast Europe's three other debutants, Julia Lopez Ramirez, Mimi Rhodes and Nastasia Nadaud, delivered in style.

England's Rhodes and France's Nadaud produced a superb performance to defeat Corpuz and Auston Kim 2&1, while the big-hitting Lopez Ramirez teamed up with her compatriot Ciganda in that final match against Korda and Lauren Coughlin.

"There's another 36 holes [on Saturday], so not every player's going to play five matches," said Nordqvist of her plans.

"Sometimes you've got to sit out someone, and for me, it was important to play all 12 players [on Friday], and the way the pairings worked out, that's how I had to play it."

During the build-up Nordqvist and Stanford both spoke of using the Solheim Cup as an advertisement for women's golf.

And the levels of skill, drama and grit on display only served to underline those comments, with the American players also poignantly wearing custom pins to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks.

"I just told them that I was proud of them again," said Stanford after the conclusion of play.

"We took a big swing from them. When you send Charley and Lottie out first, both sessions, we took some of their best body blows today.

"I'm excited because I feel like we're a heavyweight fighter. We fight with our mentality and we're just going to see how long we can last, and I feel pretty good about how long we can go."

Korda in particular set the tone early on Friday with her fifth win with Corpuz, equalling the points record for pairings set by Europe's Alison Nicholas and Laura Davies.

The US pairing of Alison Lee and Coughlin were always in control against Nanna Koerstz Madsen and Celine Boutier, taking their foursomes match 3&2 as the US opened a 2-0 lead.

An out of sorts Koerstz Madsen, who talked to her coach between sessions about her swing, and Boutier were also later on the end of a 5&3 demolition in an encounter that marked Megan Khang's sixth consecutive win in Solheim matches and her eighth in the past nine - this time alongside the metronomic Alison Lee.

Europe's fightback in the opening session was initiated by Swedish duo Maja Stark and Linn Grant who defeated Rose Zhang and Jennifer Kupcho 3&2.

Leona Maguire and Esther Henseleit followed that up by holding their nerve to defeat Andrea Lee and Lindy Duncan in another match that went down the 18th.

The victory meant Maguire improved her career Solheim Cup record to nine wins, three defeats and one halved match, to give her the highest winning percentage o any European player that has played five matches.

On Saturday, eight more points will be available across the foursomes (alternate shot) and fourballs formats, before the singles on Sunday, which will involve all 12 players on each team.

Europe require 14½ points to regain the cup, while US need 14 points to retain it.

articles.title: Lowry vuela alto en casa, pero Rahm no ha dicho su última palabra
articles.standfirst: Sensacional ronda de 62 golpes del irlandés en el Irish Open; Jon entrega una tarjeta de 67
articles.summary: Sensacional ronda de 62 golpes del irlandés en el Irish Open; Jon entrega una tarjeta de 67
articles.body: A veces una buena vuelta puede parecer poca cosa dependiendo de quién juegue a tu lado. Jon Rahm (-3) firmó este viernes un notable 67 en Doonbeg, tres golpes bajo par, en un campo que por sus características y por la influencia del viento no regala absolutamente nada a nadie. Pero tuvo que contemplar en primera fila una de esas jornadas en las que hay alguien a quien le sale sale. Su compañero de partido Shane Lowry (-11) se marcó un espectacular 62, ocho bajo par, para escaparse al frente del Amgen Irish Open con tres golpes de ventaja respecto a sus inmediatos perseguidores. El irlandés vuela en casa, aunque Rahm no parece dispuesto a haber dicho su última palabra. Ocho golpes separan a ambos cuando quedan 36 hoyos por delante. Son muchos, está claro, pero el golfista de Barrika dejó sensaciones bastante mejores que en su estreno. Sobre todo por su capacidad para no perder la paciencia cuando la vuelta amenazó con torcerse. Rahm hizo birdie en el 2 y volvió a restar en el par cinco del 8. Llegó al 9 con opciones de seguir avanzando y terminó viviendo una de esas situaciones difíciles de explicar: pateó desde unos nueve metros para birdie y salió del green con bogey. Una lástima porque pasó de lo que habría sido un gran impulso a tener que volver a remar. Tampoco aprovechó el español el par cinco del 10. Alcanzó el green de dos y dispuso de un putt de unos siete metros para eagle, pero se marchó con par. En apenas dos hoyos se le habían escapado varias oportunidades y, con Lowry acelerando a su lado, el torneo podía empezar a quedar demasiado lejos. Pero Rahm reaccionó. Dejó una gran salida en el par tres del 11 y firmó el birdie. Desde ese momento no volvió a fallar un green en regulación. En el 14, otro par tres, dejó la bola a poco más de un metro para sumar el cuarto birdie del día. El resto fueron pares hasta completar un 67 que lo mantiene con opciones de meterse en la pelea si consigue acercarse el sábado. El problema para todos es que Lowry ha puesto el listón muy alto. El irlandés salió con tres bajo par y convirtió Doonbeg en un campo completamente distinto al que había castigado a buena parte del turno de tarde el jueves. Después de dejar escapar una buena ocasión en el 2, encadenó una secuencia demoledora y jugó ocho bajo par entre los hoyos 3 y 12. El 62 lo llevó hasta un resultado acumulado de 11 bajo par y le permite afrontar el fin de semana con tres golpes sobre Haotong Li (-8), Jacob Skov Olesen (-8) y Niklas Nørgaard (-8). La cifra tiene además historia para Lowry. La anterior ocasión en la que había firmado un 62 en una segunda jornada del Irish Open fue en 2009, cuando todavía era amateur. Dos días después ganó el torneo. Diecisiete años más tarde vuelve a ponerse al frente con el mismo número de golpes y de nuevo con 36 hoyos por disputar. Quien no pudo acompañar esta tremenda aceleración fue Joaquin Niemann (-5). El chileno, líder después de su 65 del jueves, se conformó con el par del campo y ahora está a seis golpes de la cabeza. Patrick Reed (-4), líder de la Race to Dubai y compañero de partido de Rahm y Lowry, entregó un 68. Y Rory McIlroy (-2), defensor del título, repitió el 69 del jueves y necesitará también una remontada importante durante el día del movimiento para darse alguna opción de cara al domingo. La segunda jornada dejó además varias remontadas españolas alrededor de un corte, situado en uno sobre par. La más llamativa fue la de Sergio García (PAR). Después del 75 del jueves, el castellonense se sacó un 65, diez golpes menos de un día para otro, para darle completamente la vuelta a su situación. Algo parecido hizo Ángel Hidalgo (+1). Partía también desde el cinco sobre par y respondió con un 66 que lo llevó justo hasta la frontera del corte. Llegó incluso a estar cinco bajo par en su vuelta antes de ceder un golpe en la recta final. En el mismo resultado que el marbellí terminó también Eugenio Chacarra (+1), que perdió un golpe en el 18 para firmar 69, mientras que Pablo Larrazábal (+1) entregó un 70. Rafa Cabrera Bello (-1) dispone de algo más de margen después de su 71, aunque volvió a dejarse un golpe en el 18, el mismo hoyo en el que había hecho bogey el jueves. Alejandro del Rey (PAR), por su parte, firmó 70. Peor suerte tuvieron Nacho Elvira (+2), Ángel Ayora (+2) y David Puig (+2), los tres a un solo golpe de la línea después de completar sus respectivas vueltas. Al igual que Manuel Elvira (+2), que después de hacer un muy buen birdie al 17 para meterse provisionalmente en el fin de semana y de llevar su bola a green con su segundo tiro del 18, se atascó con un doloroso tripateo. Más lejos terminaron Adrián Otaegui (+4), Jorge Campillo (+7) e Iván Cantero (+9). A Rahm le queda ahora una tarea complicada, pero no imposible. Ocho golpes son una brecha considerable y Lowry ha demostrado estar especialmente cómodo en Doonbeg. Pero quedan dos jornadas y el español persigue un premio que tiene un significado añadido: un tercer Irish Open le permitiría igualar las tres victorias de Seve Ballesteros. Lowry ha volado alto el viernes. Rahm tendrá que empezar a recortarle terreno desde primera hora del sábado si quiere darse una oportunidad.

articles.title: Packers lose DL Jaden Crumedy off the practice squad to Texans
articles.summary: The Packers are losing DL Jaden Crumedy off the practice squad ahead of Week 1. He's signing with the Texans.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers are losing a player off the team's practice squad ahead of Week 1. On Friday, the Houston Texans announced the signing of defensive lineman Jaden Crumedy off the Packers' practice squad.

Crumedy will replace defensive tackle Kayden McDonald, who is going on injured reserve, on the Texans' 53-man roster. Because he was signed off a team's practice squad, Crumedy must remain on the Texans' 53-man roster for at least three weeks.

Crumedy had an excellent preseason in Green Bay . During the finale, his pressure and quarterback hit forced an interception. But at a deep position group, which featured seven players making the initial 53-man roster, Crumedy was released at final roster cutdowns, and he returned on the Packers practice squad after clearing waivers.

The Packers are entering the 2026 season with Devonte Wyatt , Javon Hargrave , Karl Brooks , Warren Brinson , rookie Chris McClellan, Jonathan Ford and Anthony Campbell at defensive tackle on the 53-man roster.

Crumedy's exit will clear the way for receiver Bo Melton , who was released from the 53-man roster on Friday, to re-sign to the practice squad ahead of Sunday's Week 1 showdown with the Minnesota Vikings.

Crumedy, a 2024 sixth-round pick, spent most of the 2025 season on the Carolina Panthers practice squad. He was signed to a futures contract in Green Bay in January.
